name: spec-library
description: The spec library — every spec, readable by its owner

spec.why: Packs are JSON for machines. The owner reads them through an agent, one command at a time. The owner's audience — product owners with no technical training — cannot. The record deserves a room anyone can walk into.

stories.title: Find the spec that needs me
stories.want: to see every spec in one list with what needs me first
stories.so: I never lose track of my own record

acceptance.then: every loadable pack is listed with its stage word and revision

acceptance.when: I filter by group or type in search
acceptance.then: only matching specs remain, counts stay true

stories.title: Read a spec end to end
stories.want: the whole spec in organized tabs with its documents rendered
stories.so: I understand it without asking an engineer

acceptance.then: overview, spec, design, tasks, review tabs are present

acceptance.then: it renders as readable markdown, tables included

acceptance.when: an ID like FR-1 or D-3 appears
acceptance.then: it is a link that jumps to its card
it reopens that exact spec and tab

stories.title: Understand where things stand
stories.want: plain words, plain dates, honest states
stories.so: nothing feels like an insider code

acceptance.then: it uses the owner-words set with the engineer term one hover away
it reads as a plain phrase, precise on hover
a friendly 'not written yet' state appears (per Q-8)
counts per group show the library's health at a glance

stories.want: open questions answerable right in the library
stories.so: reading and deciding happen in one place

acceptance.then: it lands through machine admission with my claim and timestamp

stories.title: Nothing crashes the room
stories.want: old spec folders handled with grace
stories.so: the page never dies on history

acceptance.then: they are listed read-only or hidden per Q-9, never a crash

requirements.text: The library MUST list every loadable pack with stage word, revision, and title.
The list MUST filter by need-group and free-text search.
Selecting a pack MUST present overview, spec, design, tasks, review tabs, deep-linkable.
The overview tab MUST render every adjacent .md artifact as markdown (tables included), discovered not assumed.
The spec tab MUST show stories with acceptance, requirements, and questions with honest statuses.
The design tab MUST show approach, stack, and decisions with reasoning and status.
The tasks tab MUST show status, verification expectation, and evidence receipts.
The review tab MUST show verdicts with severities.
Every ID mention MUST link to its card; every requirement MUST show its covering tasks.
Stage words, dates, tooltips, and empty states MUST speak the owner-words set (per Q-3, Q-8).
Legacy folders MUST fail soft — listed read-only or hidden per Q-9, never a crash.
If Q-1 allows, open questions MUST be answerable inline through specweb-events admission.
The owner's chosen creative extra (Q-5) MUST ship in v1.

constraints.text: The page serves on localhost with no auth in v1; authentication is a platform-adapter concern.
No CDN at runtime: every asset is vendored into the engine's web directory.
The page stays engine-name-free (grep-clean) and portable: events only at the seam, so a platform adapter can host it.
Pointer-first for the product-owner audience; keyboard stays complete for power users.

design.approach: A second page joins the room: the standing surface for every pack — readable, traceable, and actionable in place. Zero engine changes; the vocabulary stays frozen, the page translates (design.md).

stack.ui: vendored page (no framework), marked.min.js for markdown

designs.title: A page of its own
designs.detail: library.html + library.js + vendored marked.min.js, served by `loom library` on 127.0.0.1:8788; the interview room untouched; grep-clean.

designs.title: The endpoints
designs.detail: GET / · /app.js · /marked.min.js · /specs (fail-soft per folder, legacy listed) · /spec/<name> · /artifact/<name>/<file> (.md only, path-guarded); POST /event/<name> admission with 400-JSON refusals.

designs.title: The pane
designs.detail: Three counted groups — Waiting on you / Moving / Done — free-text search, needs-you first, recently-updated within group.

designs.title: The detail
designs.detail: Hash router #/<name>/<tab>; five tabs; every .md rendered (marked, trusted-on-disk posture); ID tokens jump-link; requirements show covering tasks.

designs.title: The words layer
designs.detail: PO stage words with engineer tooltips; plain dates with ISO tooltips; friendly empty states; legacy read-only.

designs.title: The journey strip
designs.detail: Five lit nodes (Just started → Being shaped → In progress → In review → Done) with Waiting-on-you and Stuck flags; presentation only, vocabulary untouched.

designs.title: Acting in place
designs.detail: Open questions get option buttons (default preselected) or textarea + honest unknown; approve appears when legal; refusals surface inline verbatim; stateless re-fetch after every act.

decisions.decision: Markdown renders client-side with vendored marked.min.js (MIT, ~39KB verified), no CDN at runtime.
decisions.because: Tables and links are load-bearing in our briefs; a hand-rolled renderer risks them. The file sits in web/, grep-clean of engine names.

decisions.decision: The owner-words vocabulary map lives in the page; engine stages stay untouched.
decisions.because: Translation is presentation. The machine keeps its frozen vocabulary (status-vocabulary rev 8).

decisions.decision: Deep links are hash URLs (#spec/name/tab) — shareable, no server routing.
decisions.because: Cheap, portable, works under any adapter host.

decisions.decision: Inline answering AND approving (Q-1: look + answer + approve) reuse specweb-events/0.1 admission — the same seam as the room.
decisions.because: One admission path, published contract, platform-portable. The room keeps the born-spec interview; the library is the standing surface for both acts.

decisions.decision: The list endpoint derives from load_specpack per folder, failing soft per folder.
decisions.because: The loader is the truth of what a pack is; legacy folders must never kill the page.

decisions.decision: GETs are stateless re-reads; no long-lived pack cache in the server.
decisions.because: Answers can land elsewhere while browsing; staleness stays one refresh deep.
